content.value_statement: AI product teams often struggle to turn model APIs into focused paid tools. This skill guides product design, prompts, cost controls, validation, and launch decisions.
actual_capabilities: Explains the AI wrapper stack from user input to validated output.
Shows prompt template patterns for product workflows.
Compares model choices by cost, speed, quality, and use case.
Outlines usage metering, hard limits, alerts, and emergency shutoffs.
Describes rate limit handling with retries, queues, and user messages.
Lists validation checks for exposed keys, missing tracking, and malformed AI output.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a deployable application.
Does not manage API keys, billing accounts, or production infrastructure.
Model names, pricing, and limits must be verified before implementation.
Does not replace legal, medical, or financial review for regulated products.

use_cases.title: Frame a Paid AI Tool
use_cases.description: Define a narrow workflow, target user, input, output, and value proposition before writing product code.

use_cases.title: Design Production AI Flows
use_cases.description: Plan prompts, validation, streaming, retries, and fallback behavior for an AI feature.

use_cases.title: Control AI Operating Costs
use_cases.description: Set usage limits, track token costs, choose models, and add alerts before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Define the Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn [problem] for [users] into a focused AI wrapper product. Identify the workflow, input, output, and success metric.

prompt_templates.title: Design the AI Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the prompt flow for [feature]. Include system instructions, user inputs, output validation, retries, and user-facing error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cost Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cost control plan for [AI product]. Include model choices, token limits, metering, user quotas, alerts, and shutdown thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Defensibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether [AI product idea] is defensible. Analyze workflow integration, domain context, data advantage, UX depth, pricing, and launch risk.

output_examples.input: A founder wants an AI tool for Amazon product descriptions.
output: Recommended focus: optimize listings for a specific seller segment.
Core workflow: import product facts, generate compliant copy, validate claims, and export ready listings.
Key controls: output length limits, banned claim checks, usage metering, and cheaper models for drafts.

output_examples.input: An engineer needs rate limit handling for an AI writing app.
output: Use a request queue to cap concurrency and requests per second.
Retry temporary 429 errors with exponential backoff and clear user messaging.
Add usage logging so product limits and provider limits stay aligned.

output_examples.input: A team is choosing between fast and high quality models.
output: Use lower cost models for drafts, classification, and high volume tasks.
Reserve stronger models for complex reasoning, review, and paid premium workflows.
Track quality, latency, and cost together before making the default choice.

best_practices: Start with a specific workflow and measurable user outcome.
Validate inputs, parse outputs, and show users clear recovery paths.
Track tokens, costs, latency, and failures from the first prototype.
anti_patterns: Do not build a generic chatbot without a workflow advantage.
Do not call AI APIs from frontend code with exposed keys.
Do not trust AI output without validation for the product domain.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan focused products that use AI APIs inside real user workflows.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, product, prompt, cost, and validation guidance.

faq.question: Which AI providers does it discuss?
faq.answer: It references OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude, and general model provider patterns.

faq.question: Can it help reduce AI API costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers model selection, usage limits, metering, caching, and alerts.

faq.question: Is it useful for nontechnical founders?
faq.answer: Yes. It can frame product value, target users, workflows, and launch risks.

faq.question: Does it address AI output quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends output validation, retries, user feedback, and safer use cases.
